# php-via: Full LLM Reference

**Version**: 0.13.0 (MIT) | **Requires**: PHP 8.4+, ext-openswoole 26
**Install**: `composer require mbolli/php-via`
**Homepage**: https://via.zweiundeins.gmbh/
**GitHub**: https://github.com/mbolli/php-via
**Packagist**: https://packagist.org/packages/mbolli/php-via
**Author**: Michael Bolli <michael@bolli.us>

---

## What is php-via?

php-via is a real-time reactive web framework for PHP. It runs as a persistent
OpenSwoole server that keeps a long-lived SSE (Server-Sent Events) connection to every
browser tab. When state changes on the server, it pushes HTML and signal patches to the
connected tabs, and Datastar morphs them into the page. No JavaScript to write, no build
step, multiplayer by default.

The name "via" means "the way". From one PHP process you get server-pushed real-time
updates without WebSockets, polling or a frontend framework.

---

## Architecture Overview

```
Browser ──── GET /page ────────────────► RequestHandler  (creates Context, renders HTML)
Browser ──── GET /_sse ────────────────► SseHandler      (long-lived stream, sends patches)
Browser ──── POST /_action/:id ────────► ActionHandler   (writes posted signals, runs the action)
                                              │
                                         Application
                                         ├── Router        (route matching, reflection DI)
                                         ├── Context       (per tab: signals, actions, views)
                                         │   ├── PatchManager   (Channel → SSE queue)
                                         │   ├── SignalFactory
                                         │   ├── ComponentManager (sub-contexts)
                                         │   └── ContextLifecycle (timers, cleanup)
                                         ├── Broadcast flush (per worker, once per tick)
                                         └── Broker        (InMemory / Swoole / Redis / NATS)
```

**Public API surface**: `Via`, `Context`, `Signal`, `Action`, `Scope`, `Config`

---

## Getting Started

### Requirements

- PHP 8.4 or higher
- OpenSwoole extension 26 (`pecl install openswoole-26.2.0`)
- Composer
- Optional: `ext-brotli` for Brotli compression

### Installation

```bash
composer require mbolli/php-via
```

### Minimal counter app (complete working example)

```php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';

use Mbolli\PhpVia\Config;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Context;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Via;

$app = new Via(new Config());

$app->page('/', function (Context $c): void {
    $count = $c->signal(0, 'count');

    $increment = $c->action(function (Context $c) use ($count): void {
        $count->setValue($count->int() + 1);
        $c->sync();
    }, 'increment');

    $c->view(fn () => <<<HTML
        <main>
            <p data-text="\${$count->id()}">{$count->int()}</p>
            <button data-on:click="@post('{$increment->url()}')">+1</button>
        </main>
    HTML);
});

$app->start(); // http://localhost:3000
```

---

## Core Concepts

### 1. Signals

Signals are reactive PHP values scoped to a tab, a route, a session, the whole server or a
custom group. Their values are sent to the browser's Datastar store and kept in sync.

```php
// Create a signal with an initial value and an optional name
$count  = $c->signal(0, 'count');        // integer
$name   = $c->signal('', 'name');        // string
$active = $c->signal(false, 'active');   // bool
$items  = $c->signal([], 'items');       // array → JSON

// Read values (typed)
$count->int();
$name->string();
$active->bool();
$items->array();
$count->getValue(); // mixed, raw

// Write a value; a scoped signal (not TAB) broadcasts its scope
$count->setValue(42);
$count->setValue(42, broadcast: false);  // write without broadcasting

// Shared counters and lists: update without losing writes from other workers
$count->increment();                                   // atomic, returns the new value
$items->mutate(fn (array $list) => [...$list, $item]); // read-modify-write under a lock

// The id the browser uses
$count->id();
```

**Ids**: a signal's id is unique per tab and includes the tab for TAB signals, so always
write it from the signal object: `$signal->id()`, `bind()`, `text()` in PHP, or
`{{ count.id }}` in Twig. A scoped signal outside a component whose name and scope are
plain letters and digits keeps a readable id such as `global_count`; every other id ends in
`____` plus codes, so names that differ only in punctuation never collide. To find a scoped
signal from code outside a context (a timer), use
`$app->getScopedSignalByName($scope, $name)`.

**Who may write a signal from the browser**: Datastar posts every signal with each action.
By default TAB signals take the posted value and scoped signals are server-owned.
`clientWritable: true` or `false` on `signal()` (or `#[Signal]`) overrides this for any
scope, and `Config::withStrictTabSignals()` makes TAB signals server-owned by default.

### 2. Actions

Actions are server-side handlers registered on a context and called from the browser with a
Datastar expression such as `@post(...)`.

```php
$inc = $c->action(function (Context $c) use ($count): void {
    $count->setValue($count->int() + 1);
    $c->sync(); // push this tab's changes now
}, 'increment');

$inc->url(); // "/_action/increment"

// In HTML: <button data-on:click="@post('/_action/increment')">+1</button>

// Signal values the browser posts are written into the signals before the action runs
$greet = $c->action(function (Context $c) use ($name): void {
    $greeting = 'Hello ' . $name->string();
}, 'greet');

// Read input that is not a signal (POST body or query string)
$c->action(function (Context $c): void {
    $option = $c->input('option');
}, 'vote');
```

An action that throws answers 500 `Action failed`; the worker keeps running and the error
is logged. Registering a second TAB action under the same name replaces the first with a
warning.

Datastar cancels an in-flight request when the page sends another one with the same method
and URL, from any element. A request cancelled before it reaches the server never runs its
action. Where every request counts, or two elements post the same action for different
reasons, give each a query string or turn cancellation off:

```html
<button data-on:click="@post('/_action/send?from=button')">Send</button>
<button data-on:click="@post('/_action/paint', {requestCancellation: 'disabled'})">Paint</button>
```

### 3. Views

Views render a context's HTML. They run on page load, on `$c->sync()` and on every
broadcast flush that reaches the context.

```php
// Simple string view
$c->view('<p>Hello</p>');

// Twig template; the context's signals and actions are passed in by name
$c->view('pages/home.html.twig', ['title' => 'Home']);

// Closure view
$c->view(fn (): string => $c->render('counter.html.twig'));

// Only send a named Twig block on SSE updates
$c->view(fn () => $c->render('page.html.twig'), block: 'counter');

// Views that read per-client or fast-changing data must not use the update cache
$c->view(fn () => $c->render('presence.html.twig', ['count' => count($app->getClients())]), cacheUpdates: false);
```

Compute values inside the view closure, as above. A value computed in the page handler,
such as `count($app->getClients())` passed to `$c->view('tpl', [...])`, is frozen at page
load.

### 4. Scopes

Scope controls which contexts share signals and receive broadcasts together.

| Scope | Who shares state |
|---|---|
| `Scope::TAB` (default) | Fully isolated per browser tab |
| `Scope::ROUTE` | All tabs on the same route |
| `Scope::SESSION` | All tabs in the same browser session |
| `Scope::GLOBAL` | Every connected client |
| `"room:lobby"` | Custom string, any group you define |
| `"room:*"` | Wildcard, matches all `room:…` scopes |

```php
// Set the scope for a context
$c->scope(Scope::ROUTE);
$c->scope(Scope::SESSION);
$c->scope('room:' . $roomId);

// Join a second scope
$c->addScope('room:lobby');

// Broadcast to a scope from anywhere
$app->broadcast(Scope::GLOBAL);
$app->broadcast(Scope::routeScope('/dashboard'));  // one route
$app->broadcast('room:lobby');

// Broadcast the context's own primary scope
$c->broadcast();

// Push this tab only (no broadcast)
$c->sync();
```

A bare `Scope::ROUTE` passed to `broadcast()` reaches every route, like `Scope::GLOBAL`.
Use `Scope::routeScope('/path')` to target one route.

### 5. Components

Components are isolated sub-contexts inside a page. Each has its own signals, actions and
view. Calling the component returns its HTML, already wrapped in a `<div id="c-…">` that
php-via targets with the component's own patches.

```php
$counter = function (Context $k): void {
    $count = $k->signal(0, 'count');
    $inc = $k->action(fn (Context $k) => $count->setValue($count->int() + 1) & $k->sync(), 'inc');
    $k->view(fn () => $k->render('components/counter.html.twig')); // count and inc passed in by name
};

$app->page('/dashboard', function (Context $c) use ($counter): void {
    $first = $c->component($counter, 'first');
    $second = $c->component($counter, 'second');

    // Call the components inside the view, so every page render carries their current HTML
    $c->view(fn (): string => $c->render('pages/dashboard.html.twig', [
        'first' => $first(),
        'second' => $second(),
    ]));
});
```

In the template: `{{ first|raw }}`. Do not call a component in the page handler and pass
the string to `$c->view('tpl', [...])`: that HTML is frozen at page load, and every later
page render resets the component.

---

## Broadcasting

Inside a coroutine (actions, timers, hooks), `broadcast()`, a scoped signal write and a
message from the broker only mark the scope. Each worker flushes the marked scopes once:
at the end of the event-loop turn when it is idle, otherwise at most once per tick
(`Config::withBroadcastTickMs()`, default 25 ms). A flush renders each scope once and each
context once, and publishes each scope to the broker once.

What this means for app code:
- Views render the state at flush time. Several writes in one action produce one frame.
- A value set, broadcast and reset within one action never reaches clients.
- Patches the action queues itself (`execScript()`, `$c->sync()`) reach the tab before the
  broadcast frame.
- The action's HTTP response does not wait for the fan-out.
- Under sustained load clients get about one frame per tick and skip the states between.

```php
$app->broadcast(Scope::GLOBAL);   // marks the scope; the flush renders it
$app->flushBroadcasts();          // render the pending flush now, in this coroutine
```

`Config::withBroadcastCoalescing(false)` renders on every call, synchronously. Outside a
coroutine (CLI scripts, tests) `broadcast()` is always synchronous.
`$app->getStats()->getBroadcastStats()` reports flushes, coalesced broadcasts and flush
times per worker.

---

## Lifecycle

```php
// Server lifecycle: onStart and onShutdown run once in every worker process
$app->onStart(function () use ($app): void { /* ... */ });
$app->onShutdown(function () use ($app): void { /* runs on stop, reload and recycle */ });

// Per-client lifecycle
$app->onClientConnect(function (Context $c) use ($app): void {
    $app->broadcast(Scope::routeScope($c->getRoute()));
});
$app->onClientDisconnect(function (Context $c) use ($app): void { /* ... */ });

// Server timer: runs on one worker, once per interval for the whole server
$app->setInterval(function () use ($app): void {
    if (empty($app->getClients())) {
        return;
    }
    $app->broadcast(Scope::GLOBAL);
}, 1000);
$app->setInterval($perProcessWork, 1000, everyWorker: true); // in every worker

// Tab timer: start it in the page handler; it stops with the context
$c->setInterval(fn () => $c->sync(), 1000);

// Context cleanup hooks
$c->onDisconnect(function (Context $c): void { /* ... */ });
```

- **A closed tab is noticed at once.** A stream ends about 1 ms after the browser closes
  the connection: `onClientDisconnect` runs, the client leaves `getClients()`, and
  `onDisconnect`/`onCleanup` run after the cleanup delay (`withContextCleanupDelay()`,
  5 s by default).
- **Idle streams stay open behind proxies.** A stream silent for 15 s writes an SSE
  comment (`withSseKeepAliveMs()`, `0` turns it off).
- **A context whose stream never connects is freed** after the connect timeout
  (`withContextConnectTimeout()`, 30 s by default), running its cleanup hooks.
- **An action on a tab whose stream is down keeps it for the reconnect.** The stream
  dropped or the action revived the context: it is freed the reconnect timeout
  (`withContextReconnectTimeout()`, 60 s by default) after the last action, longer than
  Datastar's 30 s `retryMaxWait`. A context freed before its stream returns drops its
  queued patches; the revived tab gets its signals and a fresh view, not one-off patches.
- **Revival.** A tab that comes back after its context was cleaned up is rebuilt with the
  same id and the signal values it still holds, within the revival window
  (`withContextRevivalWindow()`, 10 minutes by default), instead of reloading.
- **Reconnects.** After a network error Datastar retries the stream after 1, 2, 4, 8 and
  16 s, then every 30 s, ten times in all, each time with the tab's current signals. Once
  the retries run out or the stream ends, the default shell opens a new one within 15 s.

---

## Scaling

### Several workers on one machine

```php
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Broker\SwooleBroker;

$config = (new Config())
    ->withWorkerNum(swoole_cpu_num())
    ->withBroker(new SwooleBroker());
```

Scoped signal values, GlobalState, session data, the client list, the action rate limit and
a context directory live in shared memory, so an action that lands on any worker reaches its
tab. No sticky sessions are needed. What stays per worker: PHP statics in app code, and
server-owned TAB signals. Read-modify-write on shared values loses updates between workers:
use `increment()`/`mutate()` on signals, `incrementGlobalState()`/`mutateGlobalState()` on
GlobalState, and `#[Signal(..., atomic: true)]` in the composition API. Session data values
must be serializable. `withScopedSignalTableSize()`, `withContextDirectorySize()`,
`withSessionTableSize()` and `withGlobalStateTableSize()` size the shared tables. Deploy a
new version with a full restart, not a worker reload (`SIGUSR1`).

### Several servers

```php
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Broker\RedisBroker;
use Mbolli\PhpVia\Broker\NatsBroker;

$config->withBroker(new RedisBroker('127.0.0.1', 6379));
$config->withBroker(new NatsBroker('127.0.0.1', 4222));
```

The broker carries broadcasts between servers. Shared memory is per machine, so contexts,
scoped signal values and GlobalState are not shared between servers: route each browser
session to one server with cookie-sticky load balancing.

### Capacity and memory

Measured on the website (one worker, two cores, Brotli level 4): a page view costs 1.3 to 4.1 ms
of CPU and 13 to 35 KB until its stream connects or the connect timeout (30 s) passes; an open tab
costs 570 to 650 KB with Brotli level 4, 70 to 125 KB at level 1 and 45 to 75 KB without Brotli,
mostly the stream encoder's window; a private action about 1 ms; a broadcast about 0.05 ms per
receiving tab. A broadcast to a page's scope re-renders every component on the page, so give busy
widgets a custom scope and broadcast to it, and keep presence indicators out of Scope::GLOBAL. A
view that returns '' on updates (`fn (bool $isUpdate) => $isUpdate ? '' : ...`, with
`cacheUpdates: false`) renders a static page once. Size the shared context directory for peak open
tabs plus peak page views per second times 630. The harness is bench/capacity in the repository.

---

## Shared and Persistent State

```php
$app->setGlobalState('motd', 'Hello');
$app->globalState('motd', 'default');
$app->incrementGlobalState('visits');                                   // atomic
$app->mutateGlobalState('log', fn (?array $l) => [...$l ?? [], $entry]); // under a lock

// Keep GlobalState in SQLite across restarts (written behind, every $flushMs)
$config->withPersistentGlobalState(__DIR__ . '/state.db', flushMs: 1000);
```

With shared memory in use (`worker_num > 1` or persistence), GlobalState keys are at most
63 characters.

---

## Config Reference

```php
$config = (new Config())
    ->withHost('0.0.0.0')
    ->withPort(3000)                          // default 3000
    ->withTemplateDir(__DIR__ . '/templates')
    ->withStaticDir(__DIR__ . '/public')      // serves static files
    ->withDevMode(true)                       // verbose logging, no cache headers
    ->withLogLevel('info')                    // debug | info | warn | error
    ->withBrotli()                            // requires ext-brotli and HTTPS or h2c
    ->withH2c()                               // HTTP/2 cleartext (behind a TLS proxy)
    ->withCertificate($crt, $key)             // HTTPS directly
    ->withBasePath('/app/')                   // when mounted at a sub-path
    ->withDatastarRocket()                    // Datastar + Rocket for web components
    ->withImportMap(['charts' => '/js/charts.js'], ['/js/charts.js' => 'sha384-...'])
    ->withWorkerNum(4)                        // default 1
    ->withBroker(new SwooleBroker())          // or RedisBroker / NatsBroker
    ->withBroadcastTickMs(25)                 // broadcast flush tick; 0 = every turn
    ->withBroadcastCoalescing(true)           // false = synchronous broadcasts
    ->withSseKeepAliveMs(15_000)              // SSE comment on silent streams; 0 = off
    ->withSseMaxQueuedBytes(1_048_576)        // drop element frames for a slow client
    ->withContextCleanupDelay(5_000)          // after a stream closes
    ->withContextConnectTimeout(30_000)       // free a context whose stream never connects
    ->withContextReconnectTimeout(60_000)     // keep a tab whose stream is down after an action
    ->withContextRevivalWindow(600_000)       // rebuild a returning tab
    ->withStrictTabSignals()                  // TAB signals server-owned by default
    ->withPersistentGlobalState(__DIR__ . '/state.db')
    ->withTrustedOrigins(['https://example.com'])
    ->withAllowMissingOrigin()                // accept actions without an Origin header
    ->withActionRateLimit(100, 60)            // per IP, counted across workers
    ->withSecureCookie(true)
;
```

---

## Security

- `withTrustedOrigins([...])` rejects action POSTs whose `Origin` is not listed. Outside dev
  mode a POST without an `Origin` header gets 403; non-browser clients need
  `withAllowMissingOrigin()`. The Dev Bar endpoints and the tab-close beacon apply the same
  check.
- A context only accepts actions and streams from the session that created it.
- `withActionRateLimit($max, $windowSeconds)` limits actions per IP.

---

## Middleware

php-via supports PSR-15 middleware for authentication, rate limiting, CORS, etc.

```php
// Global middleware (runs on every request)
$app->middleware(new CorsMiddleware([...]));

// Per-route middleware (chained on RouteDefinition)
$app->page('/admin', $handler)->middleware(new AuthMiddleware());

// Per-group middleware
$app->group('/admin', function (Via $app) use ($handler): void {
    $app->page('/dashboard', $handler);
    $app->page('/users',     $handler);
})->middleware(new AuthMiddleware());
```

---

## Twig Integration

`Via::getTwig()` returns the Twig environment for registering extensions. `Context::render()`
passes the context's signals and actions to the template by name, plus:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `contextId` | The tab's context id |
| `currentRoute` | The matched route, e.g. `/docs/signals` |
| `basePath` | Base URL path, always ends with `/` (default: `/`) |
| `datastarUrl` | URL of the Datastar bundle, versioned by content, e.g. `/datastar.js?v=727844adfc` |
| `importMap` | The page's `<script type="importmap">` tag, empty without Rocket or `withImportMap()` entries |

Datastar attributes in templates, with ids written from the signal objects:
```twig
{# Display a signal value #}
<span data-text="${{ count.id }}">{{ count.int }}</span>

{# Two-way bind an input to a signal #}
<input data-bind="{{ name.id }}" type="text">

{# Bind a web component's property: renders data-bind__prop.value="<id>" #}
<sb-slider {{ bind(volume, 'value') }}></sb-slider>

{# Trigger an action on click #}
<button data-on:click="@post('{{ increment.url }}')">+1</button>

{# Show/hide based on a signal #}
<div data-show="${{ loggedIn.id }}">Protected content</div>
```

---

## Web Components (Rocket, Starbase)

Rocket is Datastar's web component layer; Starbase (https://starbase.zweiundeins.gmbh) is a
catalog of Rocket components. `Config::withDatastarRocket()` makes `/datastar.js` serve
Starbase's build of Datastar 1.0.4 with Rocket (22 KB with Brotli, against 12 KB for the
plain bundle). Configure it before `new Via()`.

**One engine per page.** Components `import { rocket } from 'datastar'`, so the page needs an
import map that maps `datastar` to exactly the URL of the Datastar `<script type="module">`,
query string included, before any module script. Another URL loads a second Datastar
engine. With the option on, or once `withImportMap()` added entries, the default shell writes
both from `Config::getDatastarUrl()` (`/datastar.js?v=<10 hex digits of the bundle's
sha256>`). A custom shell uses the placeholders `{{ import_map }}` (in `<head>`, before
`{{ head_content }}`; empty without the option or entries) and
`<script type="module" src="{{ datastar_url }}">`. A Twig layout that renders the whole
document writes both itself:

```twig
<head>
    {{ importMap }}
    ...
</head>
<body>
    ...
    <script type="module" src="{{ datastarUrl }}"></script>
</body>
```

The map is an inline script: under a CSP without `'unsafe-inline'`, allow it by its sha256 or
write it yourself with a nonce from `json_encode($config->getImportMap(), JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_HEX_TAG | JSON_HEX_AMP)`.

**Own modules and integrity.** `Config::withImportMap(array $imports, array $integrity = [])`
merges entries into php-via's map: specifier => URL (absolute or starting with `/`; `./` and
`../` throw, since every page gets the same map), and module URL => Subresource Integrity
(`sha256-`/`sha384-`/`sha512-` + base64). Later
calls replace entries with the same key. Invalid entries and the reserved `datastar` specifier
throw `InvalidArgumentException`. `getImportMap()` returns the map, `getImportMapTag()` the
tag. `getDatastarIntegrity()` is the served bundle's sha384; pin Datastar with
`$config->withImportMap([], [$config->getDatastarUrl() => $config->getDatastarIntegrity()])`
after `withDatastarRocket()` and `withBasePath()`. php-via never pins it by itself: a proxy
that rewrites `/datastar.js` would break every page, since the pin covers the script tag too.

**Loading components.** Take the script tag from a Starbase component page's Installation
section (pinned version with `integrity`) and add it with `$app->appendToHead(...)`. Put the
snippet's other `integrity` entries into `withImportMap()` and leave out its `datastar`
entries. To pin a whole catalog snapshot, save `https://starbase.zweiundeins.gmbh/c/@<catalog>/importmap.json`
with the app, pass its `integrity` to `withImportMap([], ...)` and load
`/c/@<catalog>/autoloader.js` with its hash from that file (93 hashes, 6 KB per page with
Brotli). Or copy the component's files into `withStaticDir()`; `.js` and `.mjs` are served as
JavaScript.

**Binding.** Use `$signal->bind('value')` / `{{ bind(signal, 'value') }}`
(`data-bind__prop.value`) on components, and the property form for any other property
(`bind('checked')`). Plain `data-bind` binds a custom element's `value` property only if its
tag is already defined, and the `value` attribute otherwise.

**Server state.** Render the server's value into the component's attribute in the view and
post the component's `change` event to an action, which decides the value and syncs:

```twig
<sb-slider label="Thrust" value="{{ thrust.int }}" {{ bind(thrust, 'value') }}
    data-on:change="@post('{{ setThrust.url }}')"></sb-slider>
```

**Keyed lists.** The official Datastar 1.0.4 Rocket bundle crashes when a morph reorders
keyed elements that contain a Rocket component; Starbase's build fixes it, which is why
php-via serves that build.

---

## Comparisons

| Feature | php-via | Livewire | htmx + Alpine | Inertia.js | Phoenix LiveView |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Language | PHP | PHP (Laravel) | PHP (any) | PHP + JS | Elixir |
| Real-time push | ✅ SSE | ⚠️ needs Reverb | ❌ poll only | ❌ | ✅ WebSocket |
| Multiplayer scopes | ✅ built-in | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ PubSub |
| Zero JavaScript | ✅ | ❌ Alpine | ❌ Alpine/JS | ❌ React/Vue | ✅ |
| No build step | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Framework required | ❌ | Laravel | ❌ | Laravel/Symfony | Phoenix |
| Multi-worker / multi-server | ✅ Swoole / Redis / NATS | ⚠️ | N/A | N/A | ✅ |
| Persistent connection | ✅ SSE | ❌ HTTP | ❌ HTTP | ❌ HTTP | ✅ WS |

**Choose php-via when**: you want real-time multiplayer UIs in plain PHP with no
JavaScript or build tooling, or you need scoped broadcasts (route/session/global) without
an external pub/sub system.

**Choose Livewire when**: you're already in the Laravel ecosystem and don't need
server-pushed real-time without Reverb.

**Choose htmx when**: you're progressively enhancing an existing app and don't need
persistent connections or server-initiated updates.

**Choose Phoenix LiveView when**: you work in Elixir and want the original inspiration for
php-via.

---

## Common Pitfalls (Quick Reference)

1. **Hand-written signal ids**: ids include the tab and may carry a `____` suffix; write
   them from the signal object (`$signal->id()`, `{{ count.id }}`), never by hand.
2. **Broadcast shows stale data for other clients**: views that show shared state must read
   shared state (a scoped signal or `$app->globalState()`), not a per-client TAB signal.
3. **Dual state (globalState + Signal)**: scoped signals are already shared; use
   `$c->scope(Scope::ROUTE); $s = $c->signal(...)` instead of mirroring into GlobalState.
4. **Lost updates with several workers**: `setValue($s->int() + 1)` or
   `setGlobalState($k, globalState($k) + 1)` lose writes; use `increment()`/`mutate()`.
5. **Transient state never shown**: a value set, broadcast and reset in one action never
   reaches clients, because the flush renders later; call `$app->flushBroadcasts()` first.
6. **Script runs before the morph**: `execScript()` after `broadcast()` reaches the tab
   before the broadcast frame; call `$app->flushBroadcasts()` before `execScript()`.
7. **Value frozen at page load**: compute it inside the view closure, not in the page
   handler (applies to `count($app->getClients())` and to component HTML).
8. **Variable null in view closure**: add it to both outer and inner `use` lists.
9. **Stale cached view after broadcast**: pass `cacheUpdates: false` to `$c->view()`.
10. **PatchElementsNoTargetsFound**: the root element of your rendered block must have a
    unique `id` attribute.
11. **Timer fires with no clients**: guard `$app->broadcast()` with
    `if (empty($app->getClients())) return;`.
12. **Shell templates ignore Twig**: shell HTML files use string placeholders, not Twig; put
    layout logic in `{% extends %}` / `{% block %}` templates.
13. **Action returns 403**: a POST without an `Origin` header when `withTrustedOrigins()` is
    set; browsers always send one, scripts need `withAllowMissingOrigin()`.
14. **Rocket component fails or the page runs two Datastar engines**: enable
    `withDatastarRocket()`, write the map with `{{ importMap }}` (Twig) or `{{ import_map }}`
    (shell), and load Datastar from `{{ datastarUrl }}` / `{{ datastar_url }}`. Add other
    modules with `withImportMap()` instead of a second map.
15. **Two elements post the same action and one request is lost**: Datastar cancels
    in-flight requests per method and URL; add a query string (`?from=button`) or pass
    `{requestCancellation: 'disabled'}`.
